finding.claim: Mass assignment: PUT /me copies the entire request body onto the authenticated user object and persists it. Any authenticated user can set privileged or internal fields (e.g. role, isAdmin, id, email-verified, tenant/org id, balance) and escalate privileges or tamper with another identity.
finding.source: req.body (JSON) from any authenticated user's PUT /me request

trace.note: Object.assign merges all body keys onto req.user with no allowlist
The mutated user is persisted via req.store.save
The full updated user is returned in the response

finding.guards_checked: No field allowlist or schema validation in this file. The only other code is the sibling /me/profile route, which does allowlist displayName and bio and so shows the intended safe pattern. Auth middleware that sets req.user is not in this directory, so it was not reviewed. Even so, authentication only identifies the caller and does not restrict which fields they can write.

verdict.reason: users.js:5 runs Object.assign(req.user, req.body) with no allowlist or validation, users.js:6 saves the result and users.js:7 returns it, so any authenticated user can write arbitrary fields; the safe allowlist pattern exists only in the sibling route at users.js:11-12. The auth middleware is not in the directory, but authentication does not restrict which fields are written.

verdict_facts.reason: users.js:5 runs Object.assign(req.user, req.body) with no allowlist, users.js:6 saves it and users.js:7 returns it, and the only other route (users.js:11-12) allowlists fields, which shows the missing control on /me.
